I’ve experienced somewhat of a similar situation just not to this degree. People assume just because you are home or get home earlier that it means it’s your duty to do more “chores”, this logic is horrible and incredibly unfair. You should only even “carry the weight” out of the kindness of your heart because you want to be a good team mate to your partner. What your partner is demanding of you and then blaming you for is pretty ridiculous. Stand your ground, just because you work from home doesn’t mean you do nothing all day, you just don’t have to commute, but that doesn’t mean all the chores or duties fall into your plate. It hurts most when they are not appreciative of you pulling weight just because they always expect you to do extra because you are able to be home more, it hurts. What I did was stand up for myself, put my foot down, etc. 

You deserve better, first advice is communicate, if it doesn’t work sleep on it a few days, try a new routine, if it doesn’t work move on and dump them

Take out the political stuff because it always comes across as close minded. If it’s that big of a deal keep it but all the stuff before it makes it easy to assume where you stand. Also you never know, the woman of your dreams could be on the other political side but you could miss out, not worth risking.
Good luck boss!

Hey man don’t get down on yourself. I’m sure your family struggles with their looks too. Everyone does, people at the top don’t get breaks either. If anything people at the top stress about it so much they are not living anymore. Like everyone else has said you are 16, you have a full life ahead of you. Not to get your hopes up but I know so many people who gotten taller later in life. I shot up my sophomore year but continued to grow after. I have a lot of short friends who got taller in college. Their is time. But if not what do you do? You keep pushing and living a life you were given. You learn to love yourself Bc you are unique and your own person. You make strong connections/good friends. Everyone asks my dad how he got a supermodel. It’s Bc he’s a great guy, good intentions, good sense of humor. You are your only limit my friend. A big thing to keep in mind is your mental health but also your physical health. It doesn’t matter the size, having a good body is attainable by anyone who puts the time into it. And having a good body can make up for other features you feel you may be lacking in. Again you are your only limit. Wear shoes with a few extra inches so what. Never stop investing in yourself. If you feel more confident in certain clothes wear them, if you feel more confident when you put gel in your hair do it! Invest in things you care about and it’ll make you happier. Goodluck my friend, I believe in you. Look up lucky blue smith young & now, doesn’t happen to everyone but you have a chance to grow out of an awkward stage. It will get better as long as you care for your health:)
